drafts.spl: index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 Image="*\\powershell.exe" CommandLine="*-enc*" | where match(ParentImage, "(?i)[\\\\/](winword|excel|outlook)[.]exe$") AND match(CommandLine, "(?i)\\s-enc(odedcommand)?\\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine values(ParentImage) as ParentImage values(User) as User by Computer, ProcessGuid

index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 (Image="*\\powershell.exe" OR OriginalFileName="powershell.exe") | where match(ParentImage, "(?i)[\\\\/](winword|excel|outlook)[.]exe$") AND match(CommandLine, "(?i)\s[-/]e(c|nc|ncodedcommand)?[:\s]+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine values(ParentImage) as ParentImage values(OriginalFileName) as OriginalFileName values(User) as User by Computer, ProcessGuid

index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 | where match(Image, "(?i)[\\\\/]powershell[.]exe$") OR match(OriginalFileName, "(?i)^powershell[.]exe$") | where match(ParentImage, "(?i)[\\\\/](winword|excel|outlook)[.]exe$") | where match(CommandLine, "(?i)(^|\\s)[-/](e|ec|en|enc|enco|encod|encode|encoded|encodedc|encodedco|encodedcom|encodedcomm|encodedcomma|encodedcomman|encodedcommand)(\\s+|[:=])+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine values(ParentImage) as ParentImage values(Image) as Image values(OriginalFileName) as OriginalFileName values(User) as User by Computer

index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 (ParentImage="*\\winword.exe" OR ParentImage="*\\excel.exe" OR ParentImage="*\\outlook.exe") | where match(Image, "(?i)[\\\\/]powershell[.]exe$") OR match(OriginalFileName, "(?i)^powershell[.]exe$") | where match(ParentImage, "(?i)[\\\\/](winword|excel|outlook)[.]exe$") | where match(CommandLine, "(?i)(^|\\s)[-/](e|ec|en|enc|enco|encod|encode|encoded|encodedc|encodedco|encodedcom|encodedcomm|encodedcomma|encodedcomman|encodedcommand)(\\s+|[:=])+[\"']?[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine values(ParentImage) as ParentImage values(Image) as Image values(OriginalFileName) as OriginalFileName values(User) as User by Computer

gates.gate_spl: search index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 (ParentImage="*\\winword.exe" OR ParentImage="*\\excel.exe" OR ParentImage="*\\outlook.exe") | where match(Image, "(?i)[\\\\/]powershell[.]exe$") OR match(OriginalFileName, "(?i)^powershell[.]exe$") | where match(ParentImage, "(?i)[\\\\/](winword|excel|outlook)[.]exe$") | where match(CommandLine, "(?i)(^|\\s)[-/](e|ec|en|enc|enco|encod|encode|encoded|encodedc|encodedco|encodedcom|encodedcomm|encodedcomma|encodedcomman|encodedcommand)(\\s+|[:=])+[\"']?[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}") | bin _time span=20m | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine values(ParentImage) as ParentImage values(Image) as Image values(OriginalFileName) as OriginalFileName values(User) as User by _time Computer | sort 0 - count

findings.detail: Both the base filter CommandLine="*-enc*" and the where regex (?i)\s-enc(odedcommand)?\s+ require the literal substring '-enc'. powershell.exe accepts any unambiguous prefix of -EncodedCommand, so an attacker can launch it as '-e' or '-ec' (both resolve to -EncodedCommand in powershell.exe). 'powershell.exe -nop -ec <base64>' is a fully realistic variant of the second attack step that neither clause matches.
findings.fix_hint: Match the encoded-command switch as a prefix family: (?i)\s-e(c|nc|ncodedcommand)?[:\s]+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,} , and broaden the base filter to CommandLine="*-e*" (or drop the pre-filter and rely on the regex).

findings.detail: Image="*\\powershell.exe" keys only on the on-disk filename. Attack step 1 is 'spawns powershell.exe' - a copied/renamed powershell.exe (e.g. C:\Users\jdoe\AppData\Local\Temp\winupd.exe) still runs PowerShell and still carries OriginalFileName=PowerShell.EXE, but is missed. OriginalFileName is present in the data and is not used.
findings.fix_hint: Match on OriginalFileName="powershell.exe" OR Image="*\\powershell.exe" so a renamed/relocated copy still fires.

findings.detail: The where regex requires whitespace after the switch (\s+). PowerShell also accepts colon syntax '-enc:<base64>' / '-encodedcommand:<base64>'. 'powershell.exe -enc:SQBF...' passes the '*-enc*' prefilter but fails the regex because ':' is not \s+, so the event is dropped.
findings.fix_hint: Allow colon or whitespace after the switch: ...-enc(odedcommand)?[:\s]+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}

findings.detail: ParentImage regex only enumerates winword|excel|outlook. POWERPNT.EXE and MSACCESS.EXE are common macro-bearing Office hosts but are out of the stated attack_steps scope, so only noted - do not widen beyond the three named processes unless the detection idea is expanded.
findings.fix_hint: Leave as-is for this detection; if scope is intentionally the full Office suite, add powerpnt|msaccess.

evasion_events.note: Abbreviated switch -ec (valid prefix of -EncodedCommand). Fails CommandLine="*-enc*" and the \s-enc regex though it is a direct instance of attack step 2.
Renamed/relocated copy of powershell.exe. OriginalFileName still PowerShell.EXE but Image no longer ends in powershell.exe, so Image="*\\powershell.exe" drops it.
Colon-separated switch -enc:<base64>. Passes the *-enc* prefilter but the where regex requires \s+ after the switch, so it is dropped.

findings.detail: The CommandLine regex ends with the switch delimiter group (\s+|[:=])+ immediately followed by [A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}. PowerShell happily accepts the EncodedCommand value wrapped in quotes, e.g. 'powershell.exe -enc "SQBF..."' or single-quoted. After the delimiter the regex meets a quote character, which is in neither the delimiter class nor the base64 class, so the match fails and the event is dropped. This is a realistic variant of attack step 2 (the switch+base64 chain is present, just quoted) that the search misses. The prior -enc prefix, colon, and renamed-binary findings are resolved and not repeated.
findings.fix_hint: Allow an optional opening quote between the switch delimiter and the base64 value, e.g. ...(\s+|[:=])+["']?[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}

findings.detail: The base search is only index=wineventlog sourcetype=Sysmon EventCode=1 with no narrowing term; all three filters (Image/OriginalFileName, ParentImage, CommandLine) run as post-retrieval 'where match' over every process-creation event. On a real estate EventCode=1 is one of the highest-volume Sysmon events, so every scheduled 15-minute run decompresses and regex-scans all process creations. This does not change correctness but is a real cost/latency concern.
findings.fix_hint: Add an index-time narrowing TERM that cannot be evaded relative to attack_steps, e.g. constrain on the Office parents in the base search ((ParentImage="*\\winword.exe" OR ParentImage="*\\excel.exe" OR ParentImage="*\\outlook.exe")) before the where clauses, rather than a CommandLine keyword that would reintroduce evasion.

evasion_events.note: Same WINWORD->powershell -enc base64 chain as the real sample, but the base64 value is double-quoted. PowerShell accepts the quoted EncodedCommand value, yet the trailing regex (\s+|[:=])+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,} hits the opening quote and fails to match, so the event is dropped. The search must fire on this.

findings.detail: The CommandLine regex requires the base64 value to be [A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,} (>=20 chars) immediately after the switch. PowerShell -EncodedCommand accepts ANY valid base64 of a UTF-16LE command, and short commands produce short base64: a 7-character command or less yields <=16 base64 chars. e.g. 'whoami' (UTF-16LE, 12 bytes) base64-encodes to 'dwBoAG8AYQBtAGkA' (16 chars), and 'calc' to 'YwBhAGwAYwA=' (12 chars). An attacker running winword->powershell -enc with a short encoded command (recon like whoami, or a short stager that reads its real payload from env/registry) satisfies both attack steps but is dropped by the {20,} floor. The switch+base64 chain is fully present, just short. Lower the length threshold (e.g. {4,} on a base64 token with proper boundary) rather than assuming long cradles.
findings.fix_hint: Reduce the minimum base64 length (e.g. {4,}) and bound the token with a trailing \b or end-of-token so short real EncodedCommand values match; do not gate detection on payload length.

findings.detail: Base search is index=wineventlog sourcetype=Sysmon EventCode=1 with no narrowing term beyond the ParentImage wildcards; the three where-match regexes evaluate post-retrieval over a high-volume event class every 15 minutes. Prior finding noted this; still present. Not a correctness issue.
findings.fix_hint: Push an Image/OriginalFileName TERM (e.g. Image="*powershell.exe*") into the base search to cut retrieved events before the regex stage.

evasion_events.note: winword.exe spawns powershell.exe with -enc <base64> (both attack steps present). The base64 'dwBoAG8AYQBtAGkA' decodes to UTF-16LE 'whoami' and is only 16 chars, so it fails the regex's [A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,} floor and the event is dropped. The search must match this.
